project.name: Eigenflow
project.objective: Build a PyTorch-first, architecture-agnostic, metric-agnostic post hoc neural-network interpretability toolkit for controlled probe experiments on the relational organization of learned representations across network depth and control scale.
project.interpretive_goal: Extract structural features of learned representations so human experimenters can make empirical inferences about latent representational features.
project.primary_output_objective: Produce a ZIP archive containing a complete initial Eigenflow Git repository, including its .git directory/history, suitable for immediate use as the project repository.

included: Probe-population preparation and experimental design utilities
PyTorch model inspection and activation extraction via standard module hooks
Population-level representation capture across selected or default-eligible internal modules
Metric abstraction and built-in similarity/distance metrics
Filtration abstraction and built-in graph-family constructions
Factor/class alignment analysis using probe metadata
Cross-layer, cross-metric, cross-filtration, cross-model, cross-checkpoint, and cross-probe comparison
PCSCS compatibility as a canonical special-case preset
deferred_not_required_for_v1: Exotic graph operators beyond the initial defined set
Aggressive performance optimization beyond clean sparse-capable architecture

success_criteria.statement: A user can define a probe population, supply a PyTorch model, choose or configure a metric and filtration, select analyses, and run a reproducible experiment end-to-end.
The analysis core does not require model-architecture-specific logic after representations have been extracted.
The same representation population can be analyzed under multiple metrics, filtrations, graph operators, and structural analyses without re-extracting activations.
PCSCS can be represented as a preset/configuration within the general framework rather than as a separate incompatible implementation.
Results preserve sufficient provenance and dependency information to support comparison, regeneration, selective invalidation, and resumption.
The package supports population-level analysis across network depth and control scale, producing structural observables Q(layer, control_parameter).
The final deliverable can be unzipped and immediately used as a Git repository with package source, tests, documentation, examples, project-state artifacts, and coherent initial commit history.

constraints.statement: PyTorch handles model-specific forward execution; Eigenflow wraps extraction and performs architecture-independent downstream analysis.
Do not require the package to infer semantic meaning of arbitrary internal modules automatically.
Structural observables are empirical evidence about latent feature organization, not automatic semantic explanations.
Percolation terminology must distinguish descriptive percolation-style observables from stronger claims of literal criticality or universality.
Spectral eigenvector tracking must account for crossings and degeneracies using eigenspace-aware correspondence rather than naive sorted-index identity.
v1 should be conceptually complete rather than intentionally minimal.

terminology.definition: A deliberately constructed set of model inputs, optionally with metadata and controlled factors, used as an experimental instrument for post hoc interpretability.
An internal PyTorch module/output location where activations for the entire probe population are captured. User-facing language may say 'layer' where appropriate.
The collection Z^(l) of vector representations of all probes at one internal site l.
The pairwise similarity, distance, affinity, or kernel structure induced over a representation population by a chosen metric.
A parameterized family of graphs or weighted relational structures generated from a relational matrix as a control parameter varies.
A measurable property of a representation-induced graph/operator family, such as component count, giant-component fraction, susceptibility, spectral gap, IPR, or factor alignment.
A structural feature of the learned representation geometry/topology, used as evidence about first-kind latent representational features.
A latent feature or organizing representational property learned by the neural network, inferred indirectly from controlled structural evidence.

entities.name: PCSCS
entities.description: Progressive Cosine Similarity Classification Sifting; existing EigenFlowIO repository and special case of the broader project.

entities.name: Experiment
entities.description: Top-level declarative orchestration object containing model, probes, extraction configuration, metric, filtration, and analyses.

decisions.rationale: PyTorch already performs model-specific execution and exposes generic module inspection and forward hooks.

decisions.decision: Downstream analysis is architecture-agnostic after activation extraction.
decisions.rationale: The scientific core operates on population representation matrices rather than model internals.

decisions.decision: The default analytical object is the relational organization of the entire probe population at each internal site, not single-input activation trajectories.
The principal domain is a two-dimensional layer-by-control space, with observables Q(l, p).
Probe design is a first-class subsystem, because the probe population is an experimental instrument.
Metric and filtration are separate abstractions.
Edge density is a first-class canonical control coordinate for cross-metric comparison where applicable.
Spectral analysis is operator-based and not synonymous with Laplacian analysis.
PCSCS remains a named canonical special case/preset within Eigenflow.
v1 should implement the full conceptual architecture rather than an intentionally narrow core.
The package should support preparation/configuration tools for probe populations, metrics, and filtrations rather than only accepting prebuilt objects.
Raw structural observations and interpretive claims remain explicitly separated.
The primary project deliverable is a ZIP archive of the complete initial Eigenflow Git repository, including the .git directory and usable commit history.
decisions.rationale: The repository itself is the durable implementation artifact; specifications, documentation, tests, and examples should live inside and evolve with it.

assumptions.statement: Most v1 users will provide standard PyTorch nn.Module models whose useful internal activations are hookable.
A default broad capture policy can be defined, but actual scientific analysis may need filtering to avoid trivial or redundant modules.
Flatten can remain available for PCSCS compatibility, but no single representation reducer should be treated as scientifically universal.

unresolved_questions.question: What exact public Python API and protocol/interface signatures should be frozen for v1?
What is the default module-capture policy for arbitrary PyTorch models: literally all hookable modules, filtered eligible modules, or named structural boundaries?
What is the default representation reduction behavior when module outputs are not already 2D sample-by-feature matrices?
Which built-in metrics and kernels are mandatory for v1 versus extension candidates?
Which graph operators are mandatory for v1, particularly whether modularity and non-backtracking belong in the initial release?
What result serialization format and compatibility policy should be used for long-lived experiment artifacts?
How should analysis keyword aliases map to explicit typed analysis configurations?
